# first-line-heading

- ID: `MD041`
- Category: Headings
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: no
- Tags: `headings`
- Also named: `first-line-h1`, as in markdownlint

Comments aside, the file starts with a top-level heading or front matter title.

## Why

The top-level heading is usually the document's title.

## Options

Set them under `rules.first-line-heading.options`.

- `level` (`integer`, default `1`): Level that the first heading must have.
- `front_matter_title` (`string|false`, default `^\s*"?title"?\s*[:=]`): Regular
  expression, matched in any case, for the front matter line that gives the
  document a title, which counts as the first heading. An empty string or false
  turns this off.
- `allow_preamble` (`boolean`, default `false`): Allow content before the first
  heading.

## Fix

There is no automatic fix. Only the author can write the title.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
This guide explains how to install the tool.

# Guide
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
1:1 First line should be a top-level heading
```

This document follows the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

This guide explains how to install the tool.
```

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  first-line-heading:
    options:
      level: 1
```

Under `rules`, `first-line-heading: false` turns the rule off and
`first-line-heading: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable first-line-heading` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line first-line-heading -->
```
